h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: With batch 4-10 the effective penalty alpha/batch is largest, so raising alpha over-shrinks weights and hurts more.
At tiny lr nets are undertrained after 243 epochs and wider nets change their function faster per step, substituting for lr.
Under Adam the effective functional step grows with fan-in, so wide nets hit instability at lower lr.
Narrow 16-40-unit nets are capacity-bottlenecked, so extra layers supply capacity that wide nets already have.
With tiny lr the update count is the limiting resource, and larger batches cut it at a fixed epoch budget, worsening underfit.
With batch 4-10 Adam takes many noisy steps per epoch, so raising lr reaches instability sooner than with larger batches.
3-layer ReLU nets amplify parameter perturbations multiplicatively across layers, so higher lr destabilizes them more.
Only at mid lr can deeper nets be optimized well enough to show a capacity benefit; at low lr they undertrain and at high lr they diverge.
Weight shrinkage compounds multiplicatively across three layers and collapses the signal toward a constant predictor.
Wider ReLU nets can represent the same function with smaller per-weight norms, partially escaping a heavy L2 penalty.
